FINAL ACCEPT. The revised proof resolves the 40-vertex benchmark error, and the new owner-size condition (5b) follows from the fixed-outside lemma for arbitrary physical auxiliary components.Let  $q=\lfloor N/6\rfloor$  and  $m=N-\beta_2(B)$ , the minimum number of owner omissions. Writing  $N=6q+r$  with  $r\in\{0,2,4\}$ , the two sides of
$$N-2q-2=2\lceil N/3\rceil-2$$
take the respective values  $4q-2,4q,4q+2$ . Thus (5b) is exactly  $m\le 2q+2$ .If  $m\le 2q+1$ , any minimum omission set has matching cost at most  $\lfloor m/2\rfloor\le q$ . The only remaining value is  $m=2q+2$ . An exceptional owner cycle must then exist: otherwise each path needs  $\lfloor |P|/3\rfloor$  omissions and each cycle needs  $|C|/3$ , giving  $m\le\lfloor N/3\rfloor\le 2q+1$ . Fix minimum omissions outside one exceptional cycle. The local lemma supplies a minimum choice on that cycle with no perfect auxiliary matching, so its global matching cost is at most  $m/2-1=q$ . Equation (1) now gives  $\beta_I\ge 3b-q=\lceil8b/3\rceil$ . This uses exactly one saving.The corrected benchmark description agrees with the reconstructed graph. The  $K_4$  and four vertex-disjoint triangles cover all 16 indices, and the triangles lie in one connected 12-vertex remainder. This cover gives  $\alpha(J_R)\le5$ , while  $\{0,4,7,10,13\}$  gives equality. The restricted optimum is 21, the repair attains 22, and the exact all-helper optimum is 24. Both closing math delimiters and the attribution of tested ranges to the script are corrected.Proof scope.
